st: Cut the potatoes into thick sticks, about the width of your finger, and soak them in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain and dry them very well with a towel.
Heat the oven to 200°F (95°C) so you can keep the fries warm.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 300°F (150°C). Fry the potatoes in batches for 6 minutes until soft and pale, then drain on a rack.
Meanwhile, rinse the mussels under cold water. Tap any that are open, and throw away any that stay open or have broken shells.
Raise the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry the potatoes again in batches for 3 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Salt right away and hold them in the warm oven.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the shallots, garlic and celery for 3 minutes until soft.
Pour in the wine, bring to a boil, and add the mussels. Cover tightly and steam for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking the pot once, until the shells open.
Throw away any mussels that did not open. Stir in the parsley and plenty of black pepper.
Serve the mussels in their broth in big bowls with the hot fries alongside.

ing: or beef broth plus 1 tbsp vinegar
st: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C).
Pat the beef dry and season with salt and pepper. Toss with the flour until lightly coated.
Heat the oil and [[1 tbsp]] of the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, then move it to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and the onions with a pinch of salt. Cook for 10 minutes over medium heat until golden and soft.
Stir in the brown sugar for 1 minute, then pour in the beer and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom.
Return the beef to the pot with the broth, thyme and bay leaves. Spread the mustard over the bread slices and lay them on top, mustard side down.
Cover and bake for 2 hours 15 minutes until the beef is very tender.
Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves. Stir the bread into the sauce so it melts and thickens it, then add the vinegar. Season to taste.
Serve with fries, boiled potatoes or bread.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick sticks, a little thicker than your finger.
Soak the sticks in cold water for 30 minutes to remove starch, then drain and dry them very thoroughly with towels.
Melt the tallow with the oil in a deep heavy pot. Heat to 300°F (150°C).
Fry the potatoes in small batches for 6 to 7 minutes until cooked through but still pale. Drain on a rack and let them rest for at least 10 minutes.
Raise the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C).
Fry the potatoes again in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and salt right away.
Serve hot in paper cones with a big spoonful of mayonnaise.

ing: white and light green parts, sliced
st: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the leeks, celery and carrots for 6 minutes until softened but not browned.
Add the chicken, broth, bay leaves, thyme and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, skim off any foam, and cook for 25 minutes.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate. When it is cool enough to handle, pull the meat off the bones in big pieces, checking that it is cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Add the potatoes to the pot and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Remove the bay leaves and thyme stems. Return the chicken meat to the pot.
In a bowl, whisk the cream and egg yolks. Slowly stir in a ladle of hot broth to warm the yolks gently.
Pour the mixture back into the pot with the heat on low. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened, and do not let it boil.
Add the lemon juice, parsley, nutmeg, white pepper and more salt if needed. Serve in wide bowls with bread.

ing: white and light green parts, sliced
st: Put the potatoes and carrots in a pot, cover with cold water, add salt, and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until both are very tender.
While they cook, melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the leeks and a pinch of salt, and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft and sweet.
Drain the potatoes and carrots well and return them to the hot pot for 1 minute to steam off the moisture.
Mash them with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and the warm milk until mostly smooth, leaving a little texture.
Fold in the leeks, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Serve hot with sausages or roast meat.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and butter a baking dish.
Bring a wide pot of water to a boil with salt, the sugar and the lemon juice. Add the endives and simmer for 12 minutes until tender.
Drain the endives and press them gently so most of the water comes out. Pat them dry with a towel.
Wrap each endive in a slice of ham and lay them in the dish side by side.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk gradually while whisking, and cook for 5 minutes until thick and smooth. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Pour the sauce over the endives and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes until bubbling and golden on top. Rest for 5 minutes and serve.
Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Mix the beef, pork, chopped onion, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, parsley, nutmeg, salt and pepper gently with your hands.
Shape into 8 large balls and roll them lightly in the flour.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Brown the meatballs for 8 minutes, turning, then set them aside.
Add [[1 tbsp]] butter and the sliced onion to the pan and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the apple syrup, vinegar and broth, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the meatballs to the pan, cover, and simmer on low for 20 minutes until they reach 160°F (71°C) inside.
Uncover and simmer for 5 minutes more until the sauce is glossy and thick. Serve with fries or mashed potatoes.
Stir the yeast, [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar and the warm milk together and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, the rest of the sugar and the salt. Add the yeast mixture, eggs and vanilla and mix to a sticky dough.
Knead for 8 minutes by hand or with a mixer until the dough is smooth and stretchy.
Add the butter a few pieces at a time, kneading until it is fully absorbed and the dough is soft and glossy.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Gently fold in the pearl sugar. Divide the dough into 8 balls and let them rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a waffle iron to medium. Cook one ball at a time for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden brown. The sugar caramelizes on the plates, so keep the iron clean afterward.
Let the waffles cool a minute on a rack before eating, since the sugar is very hot.
Whisk the warm milk, yeast and sugar in a large bowl and leave for 5 minutes until foamy.
Whisk in the egg yolks, melted butter and vanilla.
Add the flour and salt and stir until the batter is smooth.
Cover and rest in a warm place for 45 minutes until bubbly.
In a clean bowl, whip the egg whites to stiff peaks.
Gently fold the whites into the batter with as few strokes as possible, keeping the batter airy.
Heat a waffle iron and grease it lightly. Pour in enough batter to fill it and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and golden.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve right away with fruit or whipped cream.
Whisk the flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, ginger, baking powder and salt together.
Beat the butter and brown sugar for 3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Beat in the milk, then add the flour mixture and mix until a soft dough forms.
Shape the dough into a flat disc, wrap it and chill for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Roll the dough out on a floured counter until it is thin, about a quarter inch.
Cut out rectangles or shapes with a knife or cookie cutter and place them on the sheets with a little space.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until the edges are deep golden brown.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then move to a rack. They crisp as they cool.
Heat the olive oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Cook the diced bell pepper and onion for 3 to 4 minutes until soft and fragrant, then cool completely.
Stir the tomato paste, paprika and sugar into the cooled vegetables.
In a bowl, mix the mayonnaise with the tomato mixture, lemon juice and hot sauce until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper and taste. Add more hot sauce if you want it spicier.
Chill for 30 minutes so the flavors blend.
Serve with fries, burgers or fried snacks.

ing: beef burger patties or merguez sausages
st: Bake the fries on a tray at 425°F for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden. Salt them straight away.
Brown the burger patties or merguez in [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat until the center reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes.
Mix [[3 tbsp]] mayonnaise with [[0.5 tsp]] garlic powder for a quick garlic sauce.
Slice the baguette lengths open and toast the inside in a hot skillet or oven for 2 minutes.
Spread garlic sauce on the bread, add the meat, lettuce and tomato, then pile in a generous handful of fries.
Drizzle with [[2 tbsp]] ketchup or more sauce, close the baguette and press down. Eat fast while the fries stay hot.
nt: Best swap: use falafel or a veggie patty for the meat. Swap sweet potato fries only if you accept a softer sandwich.
